clue.text: Common error one detected in railways

indicators.note: something detected in a place is found inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: BR is short for British Railways, the old national rail network
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frequent mistake has been spotted on the railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: BONER is chiefly American slang for a blunder; BR stood for British Railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or howler, the kind of slip anyone might make, is called this in informal speech.

clue.text: Support-charges in reverse

parts.note: to back is to support
wards are charges, people in someone's care

explanation.surface: Fees for support are being run in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in the direction behind, the opposite way round, is what this adverb describes.

clue.text: Catch all round about musical work

indicators.note: all round means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a net is used to catch fish
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A trap surrounding a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine players or voices is this kind of piece.

clue.text: Put back checks-very unlikely

parts.note: reins check or restrain a horse
tall means hard to believe, as in a tall story

explanation.surface: Restore the controls, though it seems far-fetched.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up again in place is to restore an installation, as with software.

clue.text: Offering no diversion to a contemplative girl

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
musing means lost in thought, contemplative

explanation.surface: A thoughtful young woman provides no entertainment at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives no diversion fails to entertain or raise a smile, so it is dull.

clue.text: Go easy? It's a waste of time

parts.note: to go easy is to use less
less completes the phrase use less

explanation.surface: Should we slow down? It's pointless anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no worth or purpose is pointless, so trying it wastes effort.

clue.text: Draw vehicle up in a race

indicators.note: in tells us the turned vehicle goes inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A cart pulled uphill in a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull towards oneself, or lure, is to draw.

clue.text: Free from international obligation

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, an international body
a tie is a binding obligation

explanation.surface: Released from a duty to the international community.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or bond is to set free.

clue.text: Favouring drinking?

definitions.meaning: partaking of alcohol, as in 'do you indulge?'

explanation.surface: Is liking a drink a matter of preference?
explanation.definitionFit: Pampering someone favours them; to take a drink is jokingly said to be this too.

clue.text: Ridiculed the girl in blue, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud, a sound-alike

parts.note: a Girl Guide wears a blue uniform

explanation.surface: We hear that a girl dressed in blue was mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Guides are the British counterpart of Girl Scouts, in navy uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to mock or make fun of them.

clue.text: Temperate at home, in happy surroundings

indicators.note: being in surroundings means one piece is wrapped by another
being in surroundings means one piece is wrapped by another

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone moderate in habit stays home and is cheerful about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-restrained, especially in appetite or desire, is the older sense of temperate.

clue.text: Drink that's divine in trifle

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece goes inside the other here

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little importance
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A drink lies hidden within a sweet pudding of the dessert table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' suggests the British layered pudding, but means a toy or bauble; a divine is a clergyman, here DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot mix of spirits, sugar and water is a classic warming beverage of this name.

clue.text: Powerful standards for the hymnographer

definitions.meaning: units measuring power in electrical work
Isaac ..., the English writer of many hymns

explanation.surface: Strong benchmarks set by a writer of church songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of power in physics share their name with Isaac Watts, author of many well-known English hymns.

clue.text: Dame Ellen, freshly painted

indicators.note: freshly suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous actress has just had a new coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Coated with glossy paint or vitreous glaze, as a surface may be.

clue.text: Rehearses with TV favourites

definitions.meaning: goes over again, says once more

explanation.surface: Someone practises lines while watching old television shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both say the same thing over again: practising lines, or broadcasting a show once more.

clue.text: Armoured god nothing assailed

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
O is zero, nothing
plied means assailed, as with questions

explanation.surface: A god attacked with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed in a full suit of armour is to be clad in a panoply.

clue.text: Go to bed-ghost's beginning moving around!

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Time to retire to bed, for the spectre has started stirring about.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating or revolving is going round, so it is moving around.

clue.text: Versions embodying second thoughts about apparitions

parts.note: re means about, concerning
visions are apparitions, ghostly sights

explanation.surface: Accounts that include later reflections on ghostly sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: Amended texts produced after reconsidering are updated drafts.

clue.text: Holder of power has a number in great trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the number sits within the jumbled letters
great trouble suggests the letters of great are disturbed

parts.note: some means a number of things

explanation.surface: A person in authority finds several people in serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holder of power' suggests a ruler; it is a tank of gas, a fuel for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tank storing town gas, a source of energy, is a gas holder.

clue.text: Ones that make batsmen cross

parts.note: in cricket a run scored singly has the two batsmen swap ends, crossing; it does not anger them

explanation.surface: Things that annoy cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but in cricket the two batsmen cross over each time they run.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs scored one at a time, each needing the batsmen to swap ends, are cricket's ones.

clue.text: High Church job for Jack here

definitions.text: High Church job for Jack here

parts.words: High Church job for Jack here
parts.note: a jack is a worker; the one up here fixes the tall part of a church

explanation.surface: A post for Jack in a ritualist Anglican parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Church' suggests ritualist Anglicans; it is the tall part of a church, where a steeplejack works.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall spire of a church is where a jack of this trade does repairs.

clue.text: Wild men with clubs, or in one?

definitions.text: Wild men with clubs, or in one?

parts.words: Wild men with clubs, or in one?
parts.note: primitive cavemen carry clubs; members of London's Savage Club belong to one

explanation.surface: Are these brutes waving cudgels, or gentlemen in a members' club?
explanation.walkthrough: The Savage Club is a London gentlemen's club whose members are known by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous people are uncivilised; London's Savage Club members are called by the same name.

clue.text: One way of looking at Sparta's governors

indicators.note: looking at the letters another way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A certain view of the rulers of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial governors in ancient Persia had this title.

clue.text: Advantageous to make the next one deep

indicators.note: to make here means to form something new from these letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It is worth digging the next hole deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient or useful for a purpose is beneficial, if not always principled.

clue.text: What no waiter proverbially did, going out

definitions.text: What no waiter proverbially did, going out

parts.words: What no waiter proverbially did, going out
parts.note: the proverb says time and tide wait for no man, so the tide is the one that never waits; it retreats seaward

explanation.surface: A waiter leaving his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiter' suggests a restaurant; the proverb 'time and tide wait for no man' makes the tide the one that waits for nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide flowing back out to sea is said to do this.

clue.text: Shuffle for a trick

explanation.surface: Mixing the cards to fool someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to sidestep; a cunning ruse is also a scheme of this name.

clue.text: Violent agitation in chest, or muscles

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A violent upset in the chest or muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest, or a figurative outburst of strong feeling, is a violent commotion.

clue.text: O to be a candidate for getting pickled!

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Oh, to be someone likely to get drunk!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Browning's 'Oh, to be in England'; 'pickled' means drunk, but here preserved in brine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fruit often preserved in brine is a natural thing to pickle.

clue.text: Is a Rialto booze-up the Venetian sort?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a drinking bout
a Venetian is a kind of slatted window shade

explanation.surface: Is a drinking session on Venice's famous bridge the local style?
explanation.walkthrough: The Rialto is Venice's famous bridge; 'a blind' is British slang for a heavy drinking bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of heavy drinking is informally named so, as is the slatted window shade from Venice.

clue.text: Reformed Latins opt for the soulful lover?

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Converted Romans choose the romantic idealist.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Plato, whose name gives us love of the soul rather than the body.

clue.text: Very old 'uns damn badly ordered, up to a point

parts.note: D is the mild abbreviation for damn, as in d---

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the next word are scrambled

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Elderly folk curse the poor arrangement up to a certain point.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble, shaky old people who totter are said to be this.

clue.text: Complete womanizer?

definitions.meaning: one who goes after shes, read jokingly

explanation.surface: An absolute ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute or utter, as in sheer nonsense; jokingly, one who chases women, the shes.
